doc.title: John Budd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [transcript only]

title: Buddy Charles, Muggsy Spanier's stepson, at the Acorn on Oak
summary: Budd found Buddy Charles playing in Chicago and became his friend.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Great. Well we’re due for a trip to Chicago actually.
Yes I’d certainly recommend it. And do you know Buddy Charles?

Buddy Charles is a stepson of Muggsy Spanier. And I’ve heard about him from Muggsy. I knew Muggsy pretty well and he used to talk about Buddy. And one time in the Chicago, at a meeting in Chicago, another doctor and I had a room and he said one night he said “before I go to bed let’s go out and have a nightcap.” And the back door of the Drake is on Oak Street, right across from Shanango, about half way up the block is a place called the Acorn on Oak. It’s on Oak Street. So we went up there to have one drink. We walked in there and I saw in the window an advertisement, Buddy Charles. And I thought that sounds like Muggsy Spanier’s boy. So we went in and sat there and I listened to him play the piano, and then as we finished the drink I’m walking out, I walked by and I said “would you per chance know Muggsy Spanier?” And of course he was shocked. And right away he wanted to know who I was, and I said I’ll come back and see you. And we became very good friends from that time on. And he’s a remarkable guy but his wife, Ruth is his mother but Muggsy is not his father. But I’ve seen him over and over. And just about a week ago before I came here, this thing came from the Chicago newspaper, it said the mayor declared Muggsy Spanier week or something for the whole week for Muggsy. I had it here, but it doesn’t matter. He’s now working — that place burned down or was burned down, but he’s having his week declared in Chicago. It just happened.
All right. The Buddy Charles sandwich.
